demand.compared_with_the_others: This event will draw the smallest crowd of the three because early-season women's college basketball tournament games typically attract fewer than 2,000 fans.

plan.audience: Local East Bay families, Cal women's basketball season-ticket holders, alumni and youth basketball groups, plus a small group of families and friends of the visiting teams. Few students are expected because the event falls on Thanksgiving weekend, when most are away. Most people drive and park near campus; a minority come by BART to Downtown Berkeley, or by AC Transit.
plan.attendance_reason: The sourced estimate of 1,500 matches a previous Raising the B.A.R. game at Haas Pavilion (1,382) and the low demand typical of early-season women's college basketball. Championship day may draw slightly more than day 1. Thanksgiving weekend removes most students, which offsets that. The figure is well under the 11,858 capacity.
plan.reference_reason: It uses the same station (Downtown Berkeley) and the same campus setting, and the start is a Saturday midday, so the DBRK day-game profile applies. The DBRK reference is football at Memorial Stadium, which has a larger, more regional crowd and a longer uphill walk, so the share is adjusted.
multiplier_reasons: Parking: a crowd of 1,500 on a holiday Saturday parks easily in campus and nearby structures, unlike football days. This pushes the BART share down.

Walk: Haas Pavilion is about a 10 to 12 minute, mostly gentle walk from Downtown Berkeley BART. That is shorter and flatter than the 20 to 25 minute uphill walk to Memorial Stadium, which pushes the share up somewhat.

Crowd type: local families and season-ticket holders who drive replace the regional alumni and football fan base. Students, who mostly walk, are largely absent over Thanksgiving. This pushes the share down.
Competing transit: AC Transit serves the campus edge, the same as the reference, and no special event service is expected. Net effect is about neutral.
Time of day: a Saturday noon start matches the day-game reference, so no adjustment is needed.
plan.arrival_reason: Indoor basketball has no tailgating, so arrivals cluster in the hour before tip-off and the tip-off hour. Because this is a doubleheader, fans of the championship teams arrive for the second game, which starts around 14:30. That creates some arrivals at +1h and later, and the +1h slot carries part of that.
plan.end_reason: The consolation game starts at 12:00 and runs about 2 hours. After a break, the championship game starts around 14:30 and ends around 16:30, unless it goes to overtime.
plan.departure_reason: Consolation-game fans leave early, around 14:00 to 15:00, so they fall before this curve or at its -1h slot. Championship fans leave around 16:30 to 17:30 after a short walk. A small, quickly emptying indoor arena does not produce the long football tail.
plan.weather_reason: The venue is indoors and no rain is forecast in the hours around the event. The 3.8 mm daily total is light rain at other times, and this crowd is committed and mostly drives.

other_stations.why: A few riders from the south may get off here and take AC Transit or a rideshare. It is not a practical walk.
A few riders from the north may use it and connect by bus. It is not walkable to the arena.

Afternoon lull before evening travel and event arrivals.

Rain and the event's location away from Embarcadero keep evening crowds low.

narration.advice: Travel before noon or after 6 p.m. for the quietest trains. Avoid the midday and early evening steady periods if you prefer fewer people.
